def GetPatternOnBodyDetails() -> str
"""
@ingroup PATTERN_API
@brief Get details of all patterns and their position on the human body with semantic labels and body region grouping.
Returns a JSON string with two top-level arrays, "upperBody" and "lowerBody", each
containing the pattern objects that belong to that body section.
Each pattern object includes:
- patternName: name of the pattern piece
- patternIndex: index in the real pattern list
- arrangementPosition: internal body region ID (e.g. "Arm_Front_2_L")
- semanticLabel: fine-grained garment part label (e.g. "sleeve", "bodice_front")
- bodyRegion: high-level anatomical region (e.g. "torso_front", "arm_full", "leg_back")
- patternPosition: front/back orientation derived from bodyRegion
("front", "back", "full", "side", "center", or "unknown")

Arrangement position naming convention: {Region}_{Facing}_{Zone}_{Side}
Region : body area        (Arm, Body, Leg, Wrist, Ankle, Neck, Head, Shoulder)
Facing : orientation       (Front, Back, Inside, Outside, Center, Skirt, Calf)
Zone   : vertical segment (1 = closest to torso, 2 = mid, 3 = distal)
Side   : laterality        (L = Left, R = Right; omitted for center-line positions)

Supported semantic labels:
"bodice_front"      - front torso patterns (set-in, raglan, legacy, Adidas)
"bodice_back"       - back torso patterns (set-in, raglan, legacy, Adidas)
"bodice_full"       - full wrap-around torso patterns
"sleeve"            - arm/sleeve patterns (set-in, raglan, dummy)
"cuff"              - wrist cuff patterns
"collar"            - collar/neck patterns (set-in, raglan, Adidas)
"hem"               - bottom hem band of the top
"placket"           - front placket (button/zipper strip)
"waistband"         - waist transition patterns
"pants_front"       - front pants panels
"pants_back"        - back pants panels
"pants_left"        - outer left leg panels
"pants_right"       - outer right leg panels
"pants_front_left"  - front left leg panel
"pants_front_right" - front right leg panel
"pants_back_left"   - back left leg panel
"pants_back_right"  - back right leg panel
"pants_full"        - full leg panel
"skirt_front"       - front skirt patterns
"skirt_back"        - back skirt patterns
"skirt_full"        - full skirt patterns
"cuff_leg"          - ankle cuff patterns
"pocket"            - pocket patterns
"unknown"           - unrecognized or unassigned

Supported body regions:
"torso_front" - front bodice, placket, front jacket pocket blocks
"torso_back"  - back bodice blocks (set-in, raglan, legacy)
"torso_full"  - full wrap-around bodice, hem, Adidas full body, body dummy blocks
"arm_front"   - sleeve blocks (set-in, raglan, dummy)
"arm_full"    - wrist cuff blocks (wraps around)
"leg_front"   - front pants, front-left/right pants, front skirt, pants pocket blocks
"leg_back"    - back pants, back-left/right pants, back skirt blocks
"leg_side"    - outer seam leg panels (left/right)
"leg_full"    - full pants, full skirt, ankle cuff, pants dummy blocks
"neck"        - all collar blocks
"waist"       - waistband blocks

Patterns connected through seamline pairs form a single garment piece; each piece is
classified by majority vote (torso/arm/neck -> upper body, leg/waist -> lower body,
ties default to upper body) and every member is placed in the matching array.

@return JSON string with two array keys, "upperBody" and "lowerBody", each containing
the pattern detail objects for that section. On failure (no pattern editor),
both arrays are empty so the response is always valid, parseable JSON.
"""

title: SetGradingPairedAvatar
content_description: Pair an avatar already loaded in the scene to a grading size — the API equivalent of the GUI 'Pair 3D Form' action in Object Browser - Grading. The avatar is looked up by name among the avatars currently in the scene (import it first via ImportAvatar; names via GetAvatarNameList). Pass an empty name to remove the pairing for that size — like the GUI, this also deletes the avatar from the scene (with undo) when no other grading size references it.

title: GetGraphicGradingScaleRatios
content_description: Get the per-size grading scale ratios of a graphic placed on a pattern — the values edited by the GUI 'Edit Grading' tool when clicking a graphic. Each entry is the [x, y] bounding-box scale of that size relative to the currently selected grading size (so the current size reads [1, 1]).

title: GetGraphicGradingPositionOffsets
content_description: Get the per-size grading position offsets of a graphic placed on a pattern. Each entry is the [x, y] offset of that size's graphic center from the currently selected grading size's center, in 2D pattern-window units (mm; X to the right, Y downward).

title: SetGraphicGradingScaleRatios
content_description: Grade the scale of a graphic per size — the API equivalent of grading a graphic's scale with the GUI 'Edit Grading' tool. Each entry is the target [x, y] scale of that size relative to the currently selected grading size (pass [1, 1] for the current size). The list length must equal the grading size count.

title: SetGraphicGradingPositionOffsets
content_description: Grade the position of a graphic per size — the API equivalent of grading a graphic's position with the GUI 'Edit Grading' tool. Each entry is the target [x, y] offset of that size's graphic center from the currently selected grading size's center, in 2D pattern-window units (mm; X to the right, Y downward; pass [0, 0] for the current size). The list length must equal the grading size count. Values are absolute targets — calling again with the same values leaves the result unchanged. Apply scale grading first (SetGraphicGradingScaleRatios), then position, mirroring the GUI workflow.

title: AddGradingSize
content_description: Append a new grading size to a grading rule group — the API equivalent of the GUI 'Add Size' button in Object Browser - Grading. The size is propagated through the whole grading pipeline: rule table, every graded pattern's per-point size positions (extrapolated from the last sizes), attached trims, and the pair-avatar size-combination table.

title: AddGradingSizeGroup
content_description: Create a new grading rule group (rule table) holding a single default size — the API equivalent of the GUI 'Add (And Assign) Grading Rule Table' button in Object Browser - Grading. Use it to start grading on a garment that has none, then append sizes with AddGradingSize or load a .rul file with ImportGradeRuleToSizeGroup.

title: ImportGradeRuleToSizeGroup
content_description: Load a grade rule (.rul) file onto an existing grading size group — the API equivalent of the GUI 'Open Grade Rule File' action on a rule table in Object Browser - Grading. Unlike the File-Open .rul route, which only applies when the rule name inside the file matches the patterns' grading rule name, this loads the .rul onto the chosen group unconditionally, keeping the group's pattern assignments.

title: SetGradingPairedAvatarSizing
content_description: Load an Avatar Size (.avs) file and store it as the avatar sizing of a grading size — the API equivalent of the GUI 'Add Avatar Size' action in the Pair Avatar tab. Requires an avatar already paired to that size (SetGradingPairedAvatar) that is resizable; the .avs gender/avatar ID must match the paired avatar. When the target size is the currently selected grading size the sizing is applied to the avatar body immediately; otherwise it is stored and applied on the next switch to that size. 4.x-era .avs files (format v1/v2) are not supported.

title: SetGradingPairedAvatarFromFile
content_description: Load an avatar file (.avt) and pair it to a grading size — the exact API equivalent of the GUI 'Pair 3D Form' action. Unlike ImportAvatar (which replaces the scene avatar), the file is loaded additively, so calling this with different files per size builds a size set where each grading size has its own avatar; the paired avatar activates automatically on switching to its size. An existing pairing on the size is replaced.

title: RemovePatternFromAvatarMeasure
content_description:
Detach a pattern from an avatar measure (clears its "Attach to Measure (Avatar)" Line Pins).
Companion write API to GetPatternsAttachedToAvatarMeasures. Auto-simulates so the pattern
visibly releases from the measure.

title: CutPatternAlongInternalShapes
content_description: Cut a pattern piece along its internal shape lines — the API equivalent of selecting internal line(s) in the 2D window and using the GUI 'Cut' / 'Cut & Sew' context menu. Grading, sewing, and trims are propagated to the cut pieces the same way the GUI cut does. The internal lines must form a valid cutting path (reaching the pattern outline or forming a closed shape), or the cut is rejected like in the GUI.

title: MergeSewnPatterns
content_description: Merge two pattern pieces joined by a 1:1 sewing into one pattern — the API equivalent of clicking the seam line between two sewn patterns and using the GUI 'Merge' context menu. The seam between the two patterns is removed and the outlines are joined; pattern A is the base (the merged pattern keeps A's placement). A sewing group that spans more than the two patterns or an M:N sewing cannot be merged (same as the GUI).

title: GetPatternInternalShapePoints
content_description: Get the point positions of one internal shape (internal line/shape) of a pattern. Coordinates are millimeters with Y increasing downward, measured in the pattern's PSEUDO-bounding-box frame: the origin is derived from the pattern's mesh centroid minus half the bbox extents (the frame AddGraphicStyleToPattern has always used), which on asymmetric patterns can differ from the true bounding-box top-left corner by several millimeters. It is the SAME frame used by AddGraphicStyleToPattern, AddButtonToPattern, and AddButtonHoleToPattern, so the returned points can be passed straight back as placement positions (e.g. put a button on a marked internal baseline) — but do not treat them as absolute distances from the visual bbox corner. The placement APIs anchor at the item's CENTER: a button lands centered on the point, and for AddGraphicStyleToPattern pass the point with _positionRefTypeCenter=true so the graphic is centered on it (with false, the values describe the outline rectangle instead). Note that only the coordinate frame is shared: _patternIndex here is real-pattern-list order, while AddGraphicStyleToPattern indexes the full pattern list (buttons/bindings included).

title: GetPatternBaselinePoints
content_description: Get the point positions of one baseline (GUI 2D 'Baseline' tool shape, stored separately from internal shapes; only actual baseline-type shapes are enumerated — seam-allowance dummies and internal bookkeeping shapes such as link marks, symmetry reference lines, and DXF drill-hole/chalk shapes are excluded) of a pattern. Coordinates are millimeters with Y increasing downward in the same pseudo-bounding-box frame as GetPatternInternalShapePoints (see the frame note there), so the returned points can be passed straight back as placement positions (the placement APIs anchor at the item's center — for AddGraphicStyleToPattern use _positionRefTypeCenter=true). A punch-mark (cross-mark) entry returns its single [x, y] position.

title: AddButtonToPattern
content_description: Create a button (button head) on a pattern at the given position — the API equivalent of the GUI 2D 'Button' creation tool. The button uses the current default button head style and, when the pattern is graded, inherits per-size grading positions from the adjacent pattern geometry (same as GUI creation). Not allowed on curved patterns.

title: AddButtonHoleToPattern
content_description: Create a buttonhole on a pattern at the given position — the API equivalent of the GUI 2D 'Buttonhole' creation tool. The buttonhole uses the current default buttonhole style and, when the pattern is graded, inherits per-size grading positions from the adjacent pattern geometry (same as GUI creation). Not allowed on curved patterns.

title: TraceBaselineAsInternalShape
content_description: Trace baseline(s) of a pattern into internal shapes — the API equivalent of selecting baseline lines in the GUI 2D 'Trace' tool and applying 'Trace as Internal Shape'. The traced internal lines inherit the baseline's per-size grading, so they follow the pattern's grading sizes. The original baseline is kept (same as the GUI).

title: GetButtonGradingPositionOffsets
content_description: Get the per-size grading position offsets of a button (button head). Each entry is the [x, y] movement in millimeters of that grading size relative to the button's CURRENT position (the currently selected grading size reads [0, 0]), in the 2D window world axes. Buttons are indexed in scene order (creation order).

title: SetButtonGradingPositionOffsets
content_description: Grade the position of a button (button head) per size — the API equivalent of moving a button per size with the GUI 'Edit Grading' tool. Each entry is the target [x, y] movement in millimeters of that size relative to the button's CURRENT position (pass [0, 0] for the currently selected size), in the 2D window world axes. The list length must equal the grading size count. The new positions are applied when the grading size is switched.

title: GetButtonHoleGradingPositionOffsets
content_description: Get the per-size grading position offsets of a buttonhole. Same semantics as GetButtonGradingPositionOffsets; buttonholes are indexed in scene order (creation order).

title: SetButtonHoleGradingPositionOffsets
content_description: Grade the position of a buttonhole per size — same semantics as SetButtonGradingPositionOffsets.

title: ActivateAllPatterns
content_description: Activate or deactivate every pattern piece for simulation — the API equivalent of selecting all patterns and using the GUI 3D context menu 'Deactivate (Pattern & Sewing)' (_bActivate=false, _bIncludeSewing=true) or 'Activate' back. Deactivated patterns are excluded from simulation; with _bIncludeSewing the sewing (seam line pair groups) connected to the patterns is toggled together, like the GUI menu of the same name.

title: GetPatternOutlinePoints
content_description: Get the positions of a pattern's outline points (the segment endpoints of the pattern boundary; curve control points excluded). Coordinates are millimeters from the pattern bounding box TOP-LEFT with Y increasing downward — the same frame as GetPatternInternalShapePoints and the button/graphic placement APIs. Note that only the coordinate frame is shared with the graphic APIs: _patternIndex here is real-pattern-list order, while AddGraphicStyleToPattern indexes the full pattern list (buttons/bindings included). The returned order is the outline traversal order, and the indices identify points for SetPatternPointsGradingPositionOffsets / GetPatternPointGradingPositionOffsets.

title: GetPatternPointGradingPositionOffsets
content_description: Get the per-size grading position offsets of one pattern outline point — the values shown in the GUI 'Edit Grading' Distance table. Each entry is the [x, y] movement in millimeters of that grading size relative to the point's CURRENT position (the currently selected grading size reads [0, 0]), in the 2D window world axes (Y up, so a hem graded downwards reads a negative Y).

title: SetPatternPointsGradingPositionOffsets
content_description: Grade the positions of selected pattern outline points per size — the API equivalent of selecting points with the GUI 'Edit Grading' tool and typing per-size values into the Distance table. Offsets are [x, y] millimeters per grading size relative to the points' CURRENT positions in the 2D window world axes (Y up); the entry for the currently selected grading size is the reference and is ignored (pass [0, 0]). Existing deviations of the edited points are REPLACED, matching the Distance-table semantics.

content:
```
def ReplaceGraphicStyleFromImage(_graphicstyleIndex : int, _imagePath : str, _anchor : int) -> bool
"""
@ingroup UTILITY_API
@brief Replace the image on a graphic style. All colorways that share this style are updated.
The chosen anchor point on the original graphic stays fixed in world space after replacement.

@param _graphicstyleIndex: index of the style to replace
@param _imagePath: path to the new image file
@param _anchor: anchor point to hold fixed. Accepts plain integers or Marvelous::CloApiAnchorPoint enum values:
0=Center  1=Up  2=RightUp  3=Right  4=RightDown
5=Down  6=LeftDown  7=Left  8=LeftUp
@return true if successful

@example anchor = CLOAPI_ANCHOR_LEFT_UP — wide logo replaced by tall logo, top-left pinned:

BEFORE                        AFTER
8─────────────────2           8──2  <- top-left (8) same world position
│                 │           │  │
│    OLD LOGO     │    -->    │  │
│                 │           │  │
6─────────────────4           │  │
6──4

@example anchor = CLOAPI_ANCHOR_CENTER (0) — also preserves original display size:

BEFORE                        AFTER
┌─────────────────┐           ┌─────────────────┐
│    OLD LOGO     │    -->    │    NEW LOGO     │  <- same size, center unmoved
└─────────────────┘           └─────────────────┘

@example anchor = CLOAPI_ANCHOR_RIGHT_DOWN — bottom-right corner pinned:

BEFORE                        AFTER
8─────────────────2                  8──2
│                 │                  │  │
│    OLD LOGO     │    -->            │  │
│                 │                  │  │
6─────────────────4           ───────6──4  <- bottom-right (4) same world position

"""

def RepositionGraphicByAnchor(_colorwayIndex : int, _graphicIndex : int, _patternIndex : int, _anchorPoint : CloApiAnchorPoint, _x : float, _y : float) -> bool
"""
@ingroup UTILITY_API
@brief Repositions a graphic so the specified anchor point lands at (_x, _y) for a specific colorway.
@param _colorwayIndex: Target colorway index.
@param _graphicIndex: The index corresponding to the graphic style list.
@param _patternIndex: The index of the pattern piece.
@param _anchorPoint: Anchor point to pin (int value or CloApiAnchorPoint enum both accepted) -- see table below.
@param _x: Target X coordinate for the anchor point in 2D pattern-local space.
@param _y: Target Y coordinate for the anchor point in 2D pattern-local space.
@return true if the position was updated successfully, false otherwise.
@code
Anchor layout (Y increases upward):

8---1---2
|       |
7   0   3
|       |
6---5---4

Value | Enum                      | Position
------+---------------------------+---------------------
0   | CLOAPI_ANCHOR_CENTER      | center
1   | CLOAPI_ANCHOR_UP          | top edge midpoint
2   | CLOAPI_ANCHOR_RIGHT_UP    | top-right corner
3   | CLOAPI_ANCHOR_RIGHT       | right edge midpoint
4   | CLOAPI_ANCHOR_RIGHT_DOWN  | bottom-right corner
5   | CLOAPI_ANCHOR_DOWN        | bottom edge midpoint
6   | CLOAPI_ANCHOR_LEFT_DOWN   | bottom-left corner
7   | CLOAPI_ANCHOR_LEFT        | left edge midpoint
8   | CLOAPI_ANCHOR_LEFT_UP     | top-left corner

The graphic is translated so the chosen anchor point lands
exactly at (_x, _y). Size and rotation are unchanged.
Same convention as ReplaceGraphicStyleFromImage _anchor.
@endcode
"""

```

def GenerateZippersFromObj(_outputFilePathWithExt : str, _options : ObjRegisterOptions, _zipperIndex : int) -> bool
"""
@ingroup UTILITY_API
@brief Generates a zipper part asset file from one or two OBJ files, mirroring the full
"Register OBJ" dialog (DialogRegisterZipperObject) without any UI interaction.
Supports all 7 object types:
- 0: ZIPPER_OBJECT_SLIDER                → .zsl (single OBJ, single shape)
- 1: ZIPPER_OBJECT_PULLER                → .zpu (single OBJ, single shape)
- 2: ZIPPER_OBJECT_SLIDER_PULLER         → .zss (single OBJ, dual shape; mesh auto-assignment fallback)
- 3: ZIPPER_OBJECT_TEETH                 → .zth (single OBJ, fixed internal axes)
- 4: ZIPPER_OBJECT_TOP_STOPPER           → .zst (dual OBJ, dual shape)
- 5: ZIPPER_OBJECT_BOTTOM_OPEN_STOPPER   → .zst (dual OBJ, dual shape)
- 6: ZIPPER_OBJECT_BOTTOM_CLOSED_STOPPER → .zst (single OBJ, single shape)
For ZIPPER_OBJECT_SLIDER_PULLER, mesh assignment follows this fallback hierarchy:
1. User Explicit: OBJ group names listed in ObjRegisterOptions::sliderMeshNames / pullerMeshNames.
2. CLO Default: mesh names containing "slider" or "puller" (case-insensitive).
3. Dimensional: the mesh with the larger bounding-box extent is classified as Puller.
4. Alphabetical: sorted names; index 0 = Slider, index 1 = Puller.
NOTE: ZIPPER_OBJECT_TEETH ignores user-defined axis settings (axes are fixed internally).
@param _outputFilePathWithExt: Full output file path including the extension matching the object type.
@param _options: Full set of registration options (see ObjRegisterOptions).
@param _zipperIndex: Index of the zipper style in the Object Browser to assign the registered file to after saving. -1 = do not assign.
@return true on success; false if validation fails, OBJ loading fails, or saving fails.
"""

```

def GetObjectBrowserItems(objectBrowserContextOptions : ObjectBrowserContextOptions) -> str
"""
@brief Returns the Object Browser item list for a single asset type (one type per call), as a JSON string.
The asset type is given by objectBrowserContextOptions.type; supported values are OB_TYPE_FABRIC,
OB_TYPE_GRAPHIC, OB_TYPE_BUTTON, OB_TYPE_BUTTON_HOLE, OB_TYPE_TRIM, OB_TYPE_PUCKERING, OB_TYPE_ZIPPER, OB_TYPE_TOPSTITCH. The two filters are
independent: showAllColorways (tri-state) scopes the "used" check - -1 (default) follows the app's UI
"Show All Colorways" toggle, 0 forces the single colorway (colorwayIndex), 1 forces all colorways - and
bIncludeUnusedObjects additionally keeps free/unused objects (not used by any colorway) when true.
folderName is FABRIC-only: it scopes the result to one Object Browser folder. Empty = the primary/root
folder; a non-empty name = that folder (an unknown name yields an empty list). It composes with the
colorway filters and with bIncludePrints.
bIncludePrints is FABRIC-only: when true the fabric response carries print info per fabric (see @return).
@return JSON object string: { "ObjectType": "<type>", "ObjectNameList": ["name", ...] }. An unsupported
targetObjectType yields { "ObjectType": "", "ObjectNameList": [] }; an empty list is returned as [].
FABRIC with bIncludePrints == true keeps the SAME top-level "ObjectNameList" key, but its entries are
objects instead of plain names: { "ObjectType": "Fabric Prints", "ObjectNameList": [ { "Name": "<fabric>" [, "PrintName": "<print>"] }, ... ] };
the "PrintName" key is present only for fabrics that actually have a print.
"""

```
